text:
kai: FYI customer (AcmeHealth) opened an escalation — invoice token count is ~18% higher than the private meter counts. They say dashboard shows ~1.2M tokens for March but our meter only recorded ~1.0M. Asking for quick triage.

maria-support: ack, can you paste the exact invoice lines + customer ledger snapshot?

kai: dropped snippet: `invoice_id: INV-33421, period: 2026-03-01..2026-03-31, billed_tokens: 1204231`. Customer attached their meter snapshot from the onprem agent: `meter_total_tokens: 1002124` and the audit log shows ~1,202,200 events.

alex-sre: pinging ingest-bot to correlate ingestion events vs meter flushes. Do we have any recent agent upgrades for that customer?

ingest-bot: agent version: 2.14.0-deployed (sha: a9f3c2). Last heartbeat: 2026-03-31T23:58:04Z. Recent alerts: `agent.flush_error` at 2026-03-20T02:14:xxZ (retry success).

alex-sre: OK, initial hypothesis: agent buffered events offline and then a late flush/replay to billing ledger duplicated counts between audit export and meter aggregation window. Need the agent config. kai, can you ask customer for `/etc/redwood/metering.yaml`?

kai: customer pasted relevant parts: ```
flush_window_seconds: 3600
max_offline_queue_size: 500000
journal_rollover_ms: 600000
timestamp_source: system
ntp_policy: manual
```

alex-sre: interesting — flush_window is 1h, journal_rollover 10m. If the agent had a clock step (manual NTP) it may have replayed the journal twice across ledger reconciliation. Also the `timestamp_source: system` means event timestamps come from the host; if host clock jumped backward then the audit export may have odd ordering.

maria-support: customer says they performed a manual NTP correction on 2026-03-20 at 02:10 UTC after noticing drift. They also said their onprem infra had a host reboot after kernel update on 2026-03-21.

alex-sre: can you share a short log snippet around the NTP step? look for `replay`, `flush`, `dropped_events`, `persisted_journal` messages.

kai: from agent logs (redacted): ```
2026-03-20T02:09:58Z INFO journal.flush queued=482312 flushed=0
2026-03-20T02:10:01Z WARN system.ntp delta=-43200s step_applied=true
2026-03-20T02:10:05Z INFO journal.replay entries=482312 replayed=482312
2026-03-20T02:10:06Z INFO meter.emit tokens=482312 source=journal
2026-03-20T02:10:06Z ERROR ledger.upload 409 conflict duplicate_sequence
2026-03-20T02:10:35Z INFO journal.flush queued=30500 flushed=30500
```

alex-sre: that looks like a large replay immediately after an NTP step. The `ledger.upload 409 conflict duplicate_sequence` suggests the same events were already ingested upstream, so a second upload might have been accepted in invoice generation but deduped in internal meter aggregation. Need to confirm how billing pipeline dedupes. @lena-accounts can you confirm invoice generation dedupe rules?

lena-accounts: accounting: invoices are generated off the billing ledger which is append-only. We dedupe by event_id at invoice generation stage, but legacy pipelines historically relied on `ingest_event_id` + arrival_time window when receipts were processed. We recently backfilled a fix for replay collisions (2026-02) but only the hosted pipeline had the patch; private pipeline requires upgrade to server v2026.2 to be safe. If the customer is on older pipeline, duplicates might count toward invoice until ledger reconciliation runs.

oncall: quick check — what is customer agent's `ingest_pipeline_version`? kai: they report `ingest_pipeline: legacy-v1`.

alex-sre: root cause hypothesis: host clock step caused the agent to replay a buffered journal; that replay collided with previously uploaded events creating transient 409s and possible duplicate receipts in the older invoice pipeline. Meanwhile the local meter that customer used for their snapshot deduped locally (since it tracks journal IDs), causing the meter_total_tokens to be lower. The accounting invoice used the older export path and double-counted because it didn't apply the newer dedupe logic.

maria-support: next steps for immediate customer impact: 1) ask customer to upgrade ingest pipeline agent to v2.15+ and server to v2026.2 (maintenance window). 2) Provide a one-off reconciliation: we can run a ledger dedupe job for the invoice window to reconcile duplicates and issue a credit if confirmed. 3) Provide workaround: set `flush_window_seconds: 300` and enable `ntp_policy: auto` to reduce replay windows.

kai: customer asked for repro steps they can run in staging to validate fix. alex-sre: share these: 1) spin up a test host with agent v2.14 + legacy pipeline, seed journal with 400k events, stop network, then on host do `sudo ntpdate -s pool.ntp.org` to step clock backwards by 12 hours, restart networking — watch for `journal.replay` + `ledger.upload` 409 conflicts. 2) run same with v2.15 + server v2026.2 and observe dedupe preventing invoice deltas.

infra-eng: we'll schedule a reconciliation job — need permission from accounts to adjust invoice if mismatch >5%. lena-accounts: please confirm thresholds.

lena-accounts: confirmed: manual review required for >2% discrepancy. We'll standby for reconciliation request, please include audit IDs and example event_ids.

alex-sre: I'll draft the repro script and a small tool to extract `event_id` ranges from the journal for reconciliation. kai — can you collect the customer's journal tarball and ask for SSH for one hour so we can run diagnostics?

kai: on it. Customer granted temporary SSH; uploading logs to internal S3 and opening reconciliation ticket with accounts. Will follow up when we have results. :thumbsup:

maria-support: thanks team — please update thread with reconciliation ticket id once created. Closing loop for customer with ETA 48h.
